verifications.claim: Artemis III is currently targeted for launch in mid-2027, according to NASA.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Artemis III When 2027'; R3: 'launched by mid-2027'; R5: implies 2027 via mission description; R2: 'slated to launch sometime in 2027'
verifications.reasoning: NASA sources (R1, R5) directly support 2027 target but not specifically 'mid-2027'; R3 (Guardian) uses 'mid-2027'; attribution to NASA is broadly supported but less precise on 'mid'.

verifications.claim: Artemis III will be a crewed mission aimed at testing rendezvous and docking capabilities with commercial landers in low-Earth orbit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA's Artemis III demonstration mission in low Earth orbit will test one or both commercial landers... launch crew in the Orion spacecraft... test rendezvous and docking capabilities'; R5: identical description; R3: 'low-Earth orbit designed to test essential technologies'
verifications.reasoning: Directly and precisely matches NASA sources' description of crewed LEO rendezvous/docking test with commercial landers.

verifications.claim: As of April 2026, Artemis III launch date is scheduled for 2027.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Updated April 10, 2026... Artemis III launch date... slated to launch sometime in 2027'
verifications.reasoning: Exactly matches the date context and scheduling info in R2.

verifications.claim: As of April 2026, the Artemis III crew will launch on the SLS (Space Launch System) rocket in the Orion spacecraft and dock with a commercial lander (such as SpaceX’s Starship) in low-Earth orbit, rather than immediately landing on the Moon, as reported by Space.com.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1/R5: 'crew will launch in the Orion spacecraft on top of the SLS... test rendezvous and docking... with one or both commercial landers from SpaceX'; R2: April 2026 context; R3: 'no longer aim to land... low-Earth orbit'; R4: Starship HLS context
verifications.reasoning: Mission profile precisely supported; April 2026 from R2; no landing from R3; Starship via SpaceX in R1/R4/R5; minor outlet mismatch (SpaceNews R4 vs Space.com) but content directly supported.

verifications.claim: SpaceNews and The Guardian note that this revision follows concerns over technological readiness.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3 (Guardian): 'technical glitches... trying to do too much too soon... delays and technical problems... too risky'; R4 (SpaceNews): 'potential delays in hardware... problems SpaceX has had on Starship'
verifications.reasoning: Both named sources directly discuss concerns over tech delays/readiness prompting changes.

verifications.claim: This revision focuses on addressing delays in the human landing system (HLS).
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R4: 'delays in hardware... SpaceX... Starship vehicle, including the lunar lander version'; R1/R5: new mission tests 'commercial landers... Human Landing Systems'
verifications.reasoning: R4 links delays to HLS (Starship); R1/R5 imply testing addresses HLS issues, but not explicitly 'focuses on delays'.

verifications.claim: The actual human lunar landing has been shifted to the Artemis IV mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'The Artemis III mission will no longer aim to land on the moon... a new Artemis IV mission would set out in 2028 to land on the moon'
verifications.reasoning: Directly states shift of landing from III to IV.

verifications.claim: Artemis IV mission is now targeted for 2028.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'a new Artemis IV mission would set out in 2028 to land on the moon'
